input.story: I bought a washing machine for 28000 in January 2024 and it stopped working in February 2024. The company never fixed it despite many calls. Can I file a consumer case now?

output.masked_story: I bought a washing machine for 28000 in January 2024 and it stopped working in February 2024. The company never fixed it despite many calls. Can I file a consumer case now?

case.summary: The user purchased a washing machine for 28000 in January 2024, which stopped working in February 2024. Despite multiple calls to the company, the issue remains unresolved. They are seeking to file a consumer complaint.
case.user_goal: to file a consumer case against the company for non‑repair of the defective washing machine

timeline.event: Washing machine stopped working; made multiple calls to company requesting repair

evidence_missing: records of calls or complaint tickets
follow_up_questions: Please tell us which state and city you are located in.
Do you have the purchase receipt or invoice for the washing machine?
Do you have any warranty card or service call records (e.g., call logs, complaint ticket numbers)?

flags.message: The problem started about 2.9 years ago. The usual time limit for this kind of claim is around 2 years - it may be expired or about to expire. See a lawyer quickly.

notes: A Consumer Commission can also award compensation and litigation costs - we don't estimate that figure; it depends on the case.
Interest on delayed money may be claimable; the rate is for a lawyer/court to decide, so we don't add it here.

assessment.where_you_stand: You are a consumer who bought a washing machine for Rs 28,000 in Jan 2024 and it stopped working in Feb 2024. The defect and the company's failure to repair constitute a deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [KB:cpa_consumer_def]. You can claim a full refund of Rs 28,000. However, the problem started about 2.9 years ago, exceeding the usual 2‑year limitation period for filing a consumer complaint [KB:cpa_limitation]; this is a red flag and a lawyer should be consulted promptly.

options.title: Contact National Consumer Helpline [KB:forum_nch]
options.what_to_do: Call 1915 or file an online complaint at consumerhelpline.gov.in. Provide details of purchase, defect, and all communication attempts. Ask the helpline to forward your grievance to the company and seek a refund.
options.time: Same day to a few days

options.title: Write to the company's grievance officer
options.what_to_do: Send a formal written complaint (email or registered post) to the company's grievance officer as required by the E‑Commerce Rules. State the defect, request repair or refund, and give a 15‑day deadline. Keep a copy as proof.

options.title: File a consumer complaint with the District Commission
options.what_to_do: If the company does not respond, file a complaint on the e‑Jagriti portal (or in person) under the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Attach all documents, the grievance officer's reply (if any), and a copy of the claim for Rs 28,000. The filing fee is nil for amounts up to Rs 5 lakh [KB:cpa_fee_nil_5lakh].
options.time: 2‑4 weeks for filing, then hearing schedule varies
options.cost: nil filing fee; possible modest court costs

proof_tips: Ask the retailer for a digital copy of the invoice via email or WhatsApp.
Locate the warranty card that came with the machine; a scanned copy works.
Export your phone call logs for February 2024 and any SMS/email exchanges with the company.
If you have a service ticket number, request the company to email you the ticket details.
what_i_dont_know: Exact state and city jurisdiction, which may affect filing location.
Whether the company has already issued any written response or settlement offer.
If any additional terms in the purchase agreement limit the refund.
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: The defect occurred about 2.9 years ago, exceeding the 2‑year limitation period for consumer complaints [KB:cpa_limitation]; a lawyer can assess whether an exception applies and help protect your rights.
assessment.reply: You are a consumer who bought a washing machine for Rs 28,000 in Jan 2024, and it stopped working a month later. The company's failure to repair is a deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [KB:cpa_consumer_def]. You can claim a full refund, but the issue arose almost 3 years ago, which is beyond the normal 2‑year filing limit [KB:cpa_limitation]; this makes a lawyer’s advice urgent. First, call the National Consumer Helpline [KB:forum_nch] (1915) to get free help and have them forward your complaint to the company. Next, send a formal written complaint to the company's grievance officer as required by the E‑Commerce Rules [KB:ecom_grievance_officer] and keep a copy. If there is no satisfactory response, you can file a complaint online on the e‑Jagriti portal with the District Consumer Commission; the filing fee is nil for amounts up to Rs 5 lakh [KB:cpa_fee_nil_5lakh]. Do you have the purchase invoice or warranty card that we can attach to these steps?
